title: Mean spring volume-width association was uncertain at three Arctic gauges in 31 certified years from 1980 to 2011
abstract: We tested whether larger April-July flow volumes had wider central 60% flow pulses at Ob-Salekhard, Lena-Kyusyur and Yenisey-Igarka. We used 31 common complete certified years from ArcticGRO v20261104 in 1980-2011, excluding 2000. After linear year trends were removed, the equal mean correlation between log volume and width was 0.209. Conditional 95% five-year block limits were -0.012 to +0.391. Four of 31 circular phase assignments had at least this absolute mean. The main test gives no clear positive average relation. Adding August gave 0.337, with limits of +0.117 to +0.490; a central-half width check was also positive. These checks do not establish a relation that is stable across flow definitions. Short records, fixed windows, shared measurement errors, regulation and conditional uncertainty limit inference. This extends earlier width-trend tests with a relation across years on the same source records. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit support reproduction. Raw and annual records remain external.

display.caption: Mean detrended volume-width correlation and conditional 95% paired block limits for the primary test and planned checks. Three gauges have equal weight. Checks have no adjustment for multiple comparisons.
